cards.when: a reduced-form varest exists + credible theoretical restrictions (A/B contemporaneous or Blanchard-Quah long-run) for a full IRF/FEVD system.
cards.when_not: no credible restriction (-> #20/#21); you want robustness to misspecification or non-linearity (-> #22).

alternatives.criterion: there is no theory for A/B -> statistical/data-driven identification.
only qualitative sign priors -> set-identification.
robustness to non-linearity/misspecification or an externally identified shock (LP-IV).

output_key_fields: irf: 3D array {values,dim,axis labels} — the response to an impulse per horizon
Lower/Upper: bootstrap CI bands at ci (0 inside => not significant)
fevd: named list per variable — shares of forecast variance per shock
A/B/Ase/Bse: structural matrices + SE; Sigma.U: residual covariance
LRIM: long-run impact matrix (BQ/SVAR)
LR: LR test of overidentifying restrictions (small p => the restrictions are rejected)
interpretation_traps: Cholesky is ordering-dependent: the variable order is a theoretical assumption, not a given.
bootstrap bands measure only sampling uncertainty given the ID — they do not correct a wrong identification.
an unstable VAR (roots>=1) => explosive IRF, invalid CI; a stability post-check is required (roots).
Blanchard-Quah: the long-run restriction holds in first differences — the wrong order of integration invalidates the LRIM.
the IRF sign/normalization is a convention (a unit positive shock).
sources: Lütkepohl 2005 New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis
Enders 2015 Applied Econometric Time Series ch.5
Pfaff 2008 JSS 27(4) (VAR, SVAR and SVEC models)

cards.method: Data-driven SVAR identification (Cholesky / changes-in-vol / distance-cov / non-Gaussian ML) + HD + counterfactual + wild/mb bootstrap
cards.when: a reduced-form VAR fit without credible theory -> statistical identification through heteroskedasticity (svar_id_volatility_change), independence (svar_id_distance_covariance) or non-Gaussianity (svar_id_non_gaussian_ml); plus historical decomposition & counterfactual.
cards.when_not: exact theoretical restrictions -> #19; only sign priors -> #21; Gaussian and homoskedastic shocks -> statistical identification fails.

alternatives.criterion: exact contemporaneous/long-run restrictions exist.
only qualitative sign priors -> set-identification.

alternatives.alt: #22 local projections with an external instrument
alternatives.criterion: an external instrument/proxy for one shock (full-system ID is not needed).

output_key_fields: B: structural impact matrix (column j = the immediate response to the j-th shock)
model: the identified model handle (feeds svar_irf/svar_fevd/svar_hd/svar_cf and the bootstraps)
svar_id_volatility_change: Lambda (post-break heteroskedasticity), Lambda_SE, wald_statistic (test of equal eigenvalues)
svar_id_non_gaussian_ml: df (the t degrees of freedom of the shocks), sigma, B_stand
svar_hd: hd — the contribution of each shock to the historical path; svar_cf: actual vs counter
wild/mb boot: point/mean/lower/upper bands (default 0.16/0.84), SE, nboot, design, distr
interpretation_traps: svar_id_volatility_change wald_statistic: the identification is valid ONLY if the test REJECTS equal eigenvalues of Lambda — otherwise the shocks are not identified (a spurious B).
statistical ID identifies the columns of B only up to sign & permutation — you must label which column = which economic shock.
svar_id_distance_covariance and svar_id_non_gaussian_ml break down if the shocks are Gaussian (at most one Gaussian shock is allowed).
the stochastic routines (svar_id_distance_covariance, svar_id_non_gaussian_ml, the bootstraps) take an explicit seed (default 2025) for reproducibility.
svar_wild_boot: fixed vs recursive design; svar_mb_boot for dependent residuals.
sources: Lange, Dalheimer, Herwartz & Maxand 2021 JSS (data-driven SVAR identification)

cards.when: only qualitative expectations about the direction of the responses (sign restrictions) -> Bayesian set-identification (sampling rotations).
cards.when_not: exact restrictions -> #19; point-identified statistical identification -> #20; the rejection sampler can accept very few draws when the sign set is tight.

alternatives.criterion: exact contemporaneous/long-run restrictions.
statistical/data-driven point identification (without subjective sign priors).

alternatives.alt: #22 local projections with an external shock
alternatives.criterion: you already have an identified shock/proxy.

output_key_fields: irf_median/irf_lower/irf_upper: posterior summary bands (steps x nvar) at lower_q/upper_q
fevd_median/_lower/_upper: FEVD bands
n_keep: accepted draws; steps; nvar; type (median/mean); constrained; variables
interpretation_traps: set-identification, not point: the bands are the range of many admissible models (identification uncertainty), not the sampling uncertainty of a single model.
the pointwise median IRF does NOT correspond to a single structural model (Fry-Pagan 2011 critique).
constrained polarity/sign convention: the 1st element = the shock of interest, the sign = the direction; the wrong sign -> the inverted shock.
too few accepted rotations -> cryptic errors (ldraw/SDraws) which the wrapper translates into a gate (increase draws, relax the restrictions).
the sampler takes an explicit seed (default 12345); the plotting target is deliberately omitted — this node returns data, not charts.

cards.method: Local projections (Jordà) + LP-IV / non-linear state-dependent / panel
cards.when: IRF without a full VAR (one regression per horizon), robust to misspecification; state dependence (two regimes), external instrument/proxy (LP-IV + 2SLS), panel FE/IV/GMM; fiscal multipliers (cumul_mult).
cards.when_not: you want full-system FEVD/HD and efficiency -> #19/#20; very long horizons with little data (the local-projection variance explodes).

alternatives.criterion: full-system FEVD/HD, efficiency, lower variance at long horizons.
identification exclusively through sign priors (LP needs an already-identified shock).
a static/dynamic panel without an IRF horizon.

output_key_fields: irf_lin_mean/low/up: matrices — row = response variable, column = horizon (transposed relative to the IRF array of #19)
irf_s1_*/irf_s2_*: regime 1/2 responses (non-linear); fz: logistic switching function values
variables, hor, lags, shock_type (0=sd,1=unit), trend, confint, cumul_mult, use_twosls
interpretation_traps: confint is a MULTIPLIER, not a probability: 1=68%, 1.65=90%, 1.96=95% (Newey-West band width).
orientation: in irf_lin_mean rows are variables and columns are horizons — do not confuse it with the 3-D IRF array of #19.
the LP variance grows with the horizon -> wide bands at large h; do not over-interpret long-horizon significance.
cumul_mult=True gives cumulative multipliers, and only when lags_criterion is unset; shock_type 0 = one standard deviation, 1 = unit.
LP-IV: validity depends entirely on the instrument (relevance+exogeneity); there is no built-in weak-IV test; endog_data MUST be a data_frame, not a series.

cards.method: Bayesian Structural VAR identified through heteroskedasticity/non-normality (SV / Markov-switching heteroskedasticity / Student-t) + IRF/FEVD/HD/structural shocks + a Savage-Dickey (SDDR) identification check
cards.when: A multivariate series (K>=2) where you want a BAYESIAN structural VAR with shock identification through STATISTICAL STRUCTURE (not theoretical restrictions): sv=stochastic volatility, msh=Markov-switching heteroskedasticity (M regimes), t=Student-t non-normality. Posterior IRF/FEVD/HD/structural shocks with credible bands + an SDDR identification check (bsv_verify).
cards.when_not: Reduced-form work or forecasting suffices -> #11; FREQUENTIST data-driven identification (Rigobon changes-in-volatility, distance covariance, non-Gaussian ML) -> #20; theoretical A/B or Blanchard-Quah restrictions -> #19; sign-restriction set identification -> #21; regime-dependent DYNAMICS, not just the variance -> #150.

alternatives.criterion: Frequentist changes-in-volatility (Rigobon) identification instead of Bayesian; a point estimate + wild/MB bootstrap bands.
Plain recursive (Cholesky) identification without the Bayesian machinery.
Reduced-form dynamics/forecasting suffice (no structural identification).
Before interpreting IRF/FEVD: confirm that the statistical structure identifies the shocks (a negative logSDDR).

output_key_fields: bsv_estimate: model (the producer posterior 'PosteriorBSVAR*' handle) + B_mean/A_mean (posterior-mean structural/AR matrices) + model_type/p/K/S/burnin/thin/n_draws/seed/converged
bsv_irf/bsv_fevd: a long df (response|variable x shock x horizon + mean/lower/upper) — the posterior mean + quantile bands (default 16%/84%); horizon 0 = the impact
bsv_hd: a long df (variable x shock x time + mean/lower/upper) — the historical contribution of each shock per period (time = real ts time)
bsv_shocks: a long df (shock x time + mean/lower/upper) — the estimated structural disturbances
bsv_verify: logSDDR (a vector of length K per shock for SV/MSH; a scalar for t) + logSDDR_se (SV/MSH) or the SDDR ratio (t) + identified (per-shock logSDDR<0) + type/degenerate
interpretation_traps: SDDR sign: a NEGATIVE logSDDR is evidence AGAINST non-identification (the shock IS identified through heteroskedasticity or non-normality); a positive one means it adds no identification beyond the default lower-triangular structure. Minus infinity is VALID (strong evidence, the t model); a NaN or blank value is degenerate -> block.

The default identification is a lower-triangular B (recursive; the variable ORDER matters); the heteroskedasticity allows the exclusion restrictions to be TESTED/relaxed, it does not replace the recursive structure by default.
Degenerate diagnostics count as non-convergence: non-finite posterior draws (bsv_estimate) or a NaN/blank logSDDR (bsv_verify) -> a hard stop unless allow_nonconvergence=True.

TINY defaults (S=100, burnin=50): production runs raise the draw counts; the seed is MANDATORY (seeding the generator covers the burn-in and the retained draws across two sequential estimate calls; without a seed the run is not reproducible).
bsv_hd time axis: the labels are read as real numbers, NOT truncated to integers (1.25 would become 1 and destroy the axis); model='msh' requires M>=2.
sources: Lütkepohl H., Woźniak T. 2020. Bayesian Inference for Structural Vector Autoregressions Identified by Markov-Switching Heteroskedasticity. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 113, 103862.
Lütkepohl H., Shang F., Uzeda L., Woźniak T. 2024. Partial Identification of Heteroskedastic Structural VARs: Theory and Bayesian Inference. University of Melbourne Working Paper, arXiv:2404.11057.
Woźniak 2024 (Bayesian estimation of structural vector autoregressive models)

cards.method: Bayesian Structural VAR with SIGN + ZERO + NARRATIVE restrictions (set-identified, importance sampling; a Waggoner-Zha Gibbs sampler + a uniform rotation Q)
cards.when: A multivariate series (N>=2) with structural shocks identified through THEORETICAL restrictions: sign restrictions (IRF signs), zero restrictions (0 entries in sign_irf; importance sampling), narrative sign restrictions (historical episodes). Set-identified Bayesian work -> posterior credible bands on IRF/FEVD + a predictive/conditional forecast.
cards.when_not: Exclusion or recursive identification with a known order, or statistical identification from heteroskedasticity or non-Gaussianity -> #20/#19; purely reduced-form forecasting or nowcasting -> #11/#12; regime-dependent (nonlinear) structural dynamics -> #150.

alternatives.criterion: Frequentist data-driven ID (heteroskedasticity/non-Gaussianity) or a recursive Cholesky — there are no theoretical sign/zero restrictions.
Purely reduced-form work (forecasting/Granger) without structural shock identification.
Regime-dependent (nonlinear/smooth-transition) structural dynamics.
You want predictive/conditional forecast bands rather than structural IRF/FEVD bands (bss_irf).

output_key_fields: bss_estimate: model (the 'PosteriorBSVARSIGN' producer handle) + B_median (the posterior median of the contemporaneous B) + ess (the importance-sampling ESS) + n_draws + ess_ratio + converged + restrictions (the active restrictions) + K/p/S/seed
bss_irf: irf = a long-format long data_frame (response, shock, horizon, median, lower, upper) — the set-identified band per (response,shock,horizon), chart-data
bss_fevd: fevd = long-format long (variable, shock, horizon, median share + lower/upper)
bss_forecast: forecast is a long frame (variable, horizon, median, lower, upper) + conditional (True when a conditional forecast was supplied)
interpretation_traps: SET identification, NOT point: the IRF is a posterior DISTRIBUTION -> read the median + the credible band, NEVER a single 'true' response; the band reflects identification AND estimation uncertainty.

ESS is a degeneracy diagnostic (mirroring #68 and #61): sign-only -> ess==n_draws (uniform); zero or narrative restrictions -> ess<n_draws (importance reweighting); a very low ess/n_draws means very few valid rotations -> an UNRELIABLE posterior -> STOP (ess_min_ratio, overridable with allow_nonconvergence).
Zero restrictions are written as 0 in the SAME sign_irf array (NOT a separate argument); they trigger importance sampling (Arias et al. 2018).
Impossible/excessive restrictions -> the sampler spends an enormous time searching for a valid rotation Q (the L1 default max_tries=Inf can hang; the node uses a finite default).
Stochasticity: bss_estimate (Gibbs) & bss_forecast (predictive sampling) require a seed (identical draws were verified); bss_irf/bss_fevd are deterministic transformations of the draws.
sources: Wang & Woźniak (Bayesian structural VARs with sign, zero and narrative restrictions)
Rubio-Ramírez J., Waggoner D., Zha T. 2010. Structural Vector Autoregressions: Theory of Identification and Algorithms for Inference. Review of Economic Studies, 77:2, 665-696.
Arias J., Rubio-Ramírez J., Waggoner D. 2018. Inference Based on SVARs Identified with Sign and Zero Restrictions. Econometrica, 86:2, 685-720.
Antolín-Díaz J., Rubio-Ramírez J. 2018. Narrative Sign Restrictions for SVARs. American Economic Review, 108:10, 2802-2829.
Waggoner D., Zha T. 2003. A Gibbs sampler for structural vector autoregressions. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 28:2, 349-366.
Giannone D., Lenza M., Primiceri G. 2015. Prior Selection for Vector Autoregressions. Review of Economics and Statistics, 97:2, 436-451.

cards.method: Smooth-transition / threshold / (m)logistic STRUCTURAL VAR (nonlinear, regime-dependent dynamics) + GIRF/GFEVD/linear IRF
cards.when: A multivariate series (d>=2) whose dynamics CHANGE by regime (recession vs expansion, high vs low volatility, monetary regime) — a smooth-transition or threshold switch between M regimes. You want regime-/state-dependent generalized impulse responses (GIRF), a generalized FEVD, or the linear IRF of one regime. weight_function: relative_dens/logistic/mlogit/exponential/threshold/exogenous.
cards.when_not: Linear, time-invariant dynamics suffice -> #11/#12; SMOOTH continuous variation of the coefficients WITHOUT discrete regimes -> #146/#14; linear structural shock identification -> #20/#19; fully structural non-Gaussian identification (outside the surface).

alternatives.criterion: Linear/time-invariant dynamics suffice — there are no regimes (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready).
Smooth CONTINUOUS variation of the coefficients (NOT discrete regimes) + stochastic volatility.
A linear structural VAR — data-driven shock identification within one regime (heteroskedasticity/non-Gaussianity).
You want the linear IRF of one fixed regime rather than a regime-/state-dependent GIRF (sst_girf).

output_key_fields: sst_fit: model (the 'stvar' producer handle) + loglik/IC (AIC/HQIC/BIC) + params + transition_weights ((T-p)xM regime probabilities, chart-data) + identification (reduced_form)/p/M/d
sst_girf: girf (a named list per shock: point_est [(N+1) x (d+M-1)] + conf_ints; row 1 = the impact at n=0) + which_shocks/N/ci — regime-dependent generalized responses
sst_gfevd: gfevd (a 3D array [horizon x variable x shock]) + initval_type/N — the generalized variance decomposition
sst_linear_irf: point_est (a 3-D array [variables x shock x horizon], slice 1 = the impact) + conf_ints (wild-bootstrap bands, or absent) + regime/N
interpretation_traps: The GIRF is NON-LINEAR & NON-SYMMETRIC: the response depends on the size/sign of the shock AND on the initial state (init_regime) — NOT like a linear IRF.
linear_IRF/GIRF on a reduced-form model -> an automatic lower-triangular recursive (Cholesky) ID (the variable ORDER matters); structural without an order -> the non-Gaussian fitSSTVAR.
the sst_linear_irf bootstrap bands exist ONLY for models with linear AR dynamics; on a genuinely regime-dependent STVAR they are absent (use the GIRF).

The stochastic GA log-likelihood is multimodal: small nrounds/ngen (the defaults are TINY) -> a local maximum; production runs raise nrounds/ngen. The seed is MANDATORY (without it the run is not reproducible).

sst_fit filters out unsuitable solutions (near-singular Sigma with eig<0.002, companion modulus>0.9985); if no appropriate solution is found -> rescale the series to a similar magnitude or run more rounds.
relative_dens => a Gaussian cond_dist ONLY; logistic/exponential => M=2; a non-relative_dens weight function => weightfun_pars is mandatory (e.g. c(switch_var, lag)).
sources: Lanne M., Virolainen S. 2025. A Gaussian smooth transition vector autoregressive model. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 178, 105162.
Virolainen S. (in press). Identification by non-Gaussianity in structural smooth transition VAR models. Econometric Reviews.
Hubrich K., Teräsvirta T. 2013. Thresholds and Smooth Transitions in VAR Models. CREATES Research Paper 2013-18, Aarhus University.
Tsay R. 1998. Testing and Modeling Multivariate Threshold Models. JASA, 93:443, 1188-1202.
Lanne M., Nyberg H. 2016. Generalized Forecast Error Variance Decomposition for Linear and Nonlinear Multivariate Models. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 78:4, 595-603.
Kilian L., Lütkepohl H. 2017. Structural Vector Autoregressive Analysis. Cambridge University Press.

cards.method: Gaussian / Student's-t Mixture VAR (regime switching through mixture-density weights) + GIRF/GFEVD/linear IRF
cards.when: A multivariate series (d>=2) whose dynamics SWITCH between M regimes with mixture-density weights that depend on the past (recession vs expansion, high vs low volatility, monetary regime). The regimes are Gaussian (GMVAR), Student's-t (StMVAR) or mixed (G-StMVAR). You want regime-/state-dependent GIRF, a generalized FEVD, or the linear IRF of one regime, with optional structural ID through conditional heteroskedasticity (W).
cards.when_not: Linear, time-invariant dynamics suffice -> #11/#12; a smooth-transition, threshold or (m)logistic switch rather than mixture-density weights -> #150; smooth CONTINUOUS variation of the coefficients rather than discrete regimes -> #146/#14; linear data-driven structural identification -> #20; the univariate case (d=1) is out of scope.

alternatives.criterion: The switch is smooth-transition/threshold/(m)logistic/exogenous — NOT mixture-density weights (the closest successor).
Linear/time-invariant dynamics suffice — there are no regimes (cheaper, IRF/FEVD ready).
A linear structural VAR — data-driven shock identification within one regime.
You want the linear IRF of one fixed regime rather than a regime-/state-dependent GIRF (gmv_girf).

output_key_fields: gmv_fit: model (the 'gsmvar' producer handle) + loglik/IC (AIC/HQIC/BIC) + params/std_errors + mixing_weights (a T x M regime-probability path, chart-data) + M/d/p/model_type/structural/converged/n_converged
gmv_girf: girf (a named list per shock: point_est [(N+1) x variables] + conf_ints; row 1 is the impact at n=0) + which_shocks/N/ci — the non-linear generalized responses
gmv_gfevd: gfevd (a 3D array [(N+1) x variable x shock]) + initval_type/N — the generalized variance decomposition
gmv_linear_irf: point_est (a 3-D array [variables x shock x (N+1)], slice 1 = the impact) + conf_ints (4-D wild-bootstrap bands, or absent) + regime/N
interpretation_traps: The GIRF is NON-LINEAR & NON-SYMMETRIC: the response depends on the size/sign of the shock AND on the initial state (init_regimes) — NOT like a linear IRF
linear_IRF/GIRF on a reduced-form model -> an automatic lower-triangular recursive (Cholesky) ID (the variable ORDER matters); genuine structural ID -> structural_W (which requires M>=2)
the gmv_linear_irf bootstrap bands exist ONLY for models with linear AR dynamics (M==1, or constrained identical); with genuine regime switching they are absent (use the GIRF)
The GFEVD seeds length DEPENDS on initval_type (live-verified): nrow(data)-p+1 for 'data', R2 for 'random'; the wrapper computes it automatically

A stochastic genetic algorithm on a multimodal log-likelihood: a small ncalls (the TINY default of 2) lands on a local maximum; production uses ncalls=(M+1)^5. The seed is MANDATORY. Convergence post-gate: degenerate (no round converged, or a non-finite log-likelihood) => stop unless allow_nonconvergence=True
G-StMVAR requires M=c(M1,M2) (M1 Gaussian + M2 Student's-t regimes); Student's-t df near the boundary => effectively Gaussian
sources: Kalliovirta L., Meitz M., Saikkonen P. 2016. Gaussian mixture vector autoregression. Journal of Econometrics, 192:2, 485-498.
Virolainen S. 2022. A mixture autoregressive model based on Gaussian and Student's t-distributions. Studies in Nonlinear Dynamics & Econometrics, 26:4, 559-580.
Virolainen S. 2025. A statistically identified structural vector autoregression with endogenously switching volatility regime. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 43:1, 44-54.
Lanne M., Nyberg H. 2016. Generalized Forecast Error Variance Decomposition for Linear and Nonlinear Multivariate Models. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 78:4, 595-603.

cards.method: Desparsified/debiased LASSO inference (high-dimensional time series) + high-dimensional local projections (HDLP) with valid CIs — Adamek-Smeekes-Wilms
cards.when: High-dimensional inference: a point estimate + honest CIs + a z/Wald test for the target coefficient(s) when N (regressors) is large/≈T (dlasso_inference); or an IRF via local projection with MANY controls & valid asymptotic CIs (HAC/LRV variance) when a plain LP would be over-parameterised (dlasso_local_projection); optionally a state-dependent IRF (Ramey-Zubairy). The shock must already be identified/exogenous.
cards.when_not: A low-dimensional local projection with few controls -> #22 (OLS + Newey-West, no penalty); full-system FEVD/HD and efficiency -> #19/#20; shock identification from sign priors -> #21 (this card does NOT identify shocks, it takes them as given); pure forecasting rather than inference -> the shrinkage and ML forecasters.

alternatives.criterion: A low-dimensional LP/LP-IV: few controls, standard OLS + Newey-West bands suffice (no high-dimensional penalty/debiasing).
A full-system IRF/FEVD/HD with efficiency & lower variance at long horizons (not high-dimensional).
The shock is identified ONLY through sign restrictions; this card presupposes an already identified shock.

output_key_fields: coefficients (dlasso_inference): a frame of variable/bhat/se (debiased estimates, on the original scale)
intervals (dlasso_inference): a frame of variable + lower/upper per alpha (honest intervals)
joint_test (dlasso_inference): H0 is R*beta=q (by default all of H jointly zero) -> statistic/p_value
row_tests (dlasso_inference): the per-row z statistics + intervals (ONLY when the restriction matrix or q is supplied); n_selected: the number of non-zeros in the initial lasso
irf (dlasso_local_projection): a named list per state, each a frame of horizon + lower/bhat/upper per alpha (the interval bands — chart data)
dlasso_local_projection: states/n_states/hmax/lags/cumulate_y/OLS/seed
interpretation_traps: STOCHASTICITY (live-verified): although the debiasing is convex+analytic, the lambda selection uses RANDOM CV folds -> WITHOUT a seed two calls give different bhat. The seed is MANDATORY in both tools.
alphas is the significance level (0.05 -> a 95% CI); the column 'lower 0.05'/'upper 0.05' corresponds to alpha=0.05 (NOT the 5% quantile).
dlasso_local_projection: a hard gate requires hmax + lags < T. Beyond it the routine itself SILENTLY truncates hmax (to 0.8*eff - lags); the wrapper surfaces that as a message instead of losing it.
this card does NOT identify a structural shock — x must already be exogenous and identified (a proxy, an instrument, or an orthogonalised series). The validity of the inference rests on that.
q in dlasso_local_projection = the 'fast' controls (the high-dimensional space); q in dlasso_inference = the RHS of H0 the reference*beta=q. The SAME NAME but a DIFFERENT meaning.
OLS=True only in the low-dimensional case (otherwise the system is singular); state_variables: each column must be categorical OR a binary indicator of one regime.
sources: Adamek, Smeekes & Wilms 2021 'LASSO inference for high-dimensional time series' (arXiv:2007.10952)
van de Geer, Buhlmann, Ritov & Dezeure 2014 'On asymptotically optimal confidence regions and tests for high-dimensional models' (Annals of Statistics 42(3):1166-1202)
Plagborg-Moller & Wolf 2021 'Local projections and VARs estimate the same impulse responses' (Econometrica 89(2):955-980)
Ramey & Zubairy 2018 'Government spending multipliers in good times and in bad' (JPE 126(2):850-901); Andrews 1991 (Econometrica 59(3):817-858)

cards.method: Residual diagnostics for a reduced-form VAR: a multivariate LM autocorrelation test (+HC-robust/univariate) + a combined bootstrap ARCH test (CA/ET/MARCH) + a wild-bootstrap AC test
cards.when: After estimating a reduced-form VAR (vr_fit #11 -> varest, or the native vtt_fit -> VARfit): checking the adequacy of the residuals before structural ID/IRF. Autocorrelation (the Ahlgren-Catani multivariate LM + HC0-HC3 + per equation), ARCH/volatility clustering (the combined CA + Eklund-Terasvirta CCC-ARCH + multivariate MARCH, bootstrapped), wild-bootstrap AC p-values for a small/heteroskedastic sample.
cards.when_not: Estimating or selecting the VAR lags -> #11 (vr_fit); a cointegration bootstrap -> category 05; residual normality (this card has NO normality test); producing IRF/FEVD (it is purely diagnostics); a bare residual matrix as input (the LM auxiliary regressions need the whole fitted model).

alternatives.criterion: A small sample or heteroskedastic errors: wild-bootstrap p-values (Ahlgren-Catani Algorithm 1/2) instead of the asymptotic chi^2 of vtt_portmanteau.
The test concerns ARCH/volatility clustering in the residuals (not autocorrelation).
Autocorrelation is rejected -> increase the lags of the reduced-form VAR and re-test.

output_key_fields: vtt_portmanteau: a multivariate frame (HCtype, the statistic Q, p_value, df=K^2*h, decision) + h/K/alpha/inputType; univariate=True adds a per-equation frame (df=h)

vtt_arch: one entry per test -> CA {statistic = 1-min_i p(LM_i), boot_p, uni_stat, uni_boot_p, decision}; MARCH {statistic, asymp_p, boot_p, df=K^2(K+1)^2 h/4, decision}; ET {statistic, asymp_p, boot_p, df=K*h, decision} + B/dist/seed
vtt_wildboot: a wild data_frame (HCtype, the statistic from ACtest, WB.p, df, decision) + WBtype/WBdist/numberOfErrors/numberOfNA/seed
vtt_fit: the model handle (a 'VARfit' producer) + K/p/N/variables/residuals (chart-data)
interpretation_traps: Polarity: H0 = CLEAN residuals (no AC / no ARCH). p<alpha => reject => misspecification is present (autocorrelation/ARCH) => the VAR FAILS the test (not the other way round).
vtt_arch & vtt_wildboot are bootstrap-based => the seed is MANDATORY; the same seed => the same bootstrap p-values (cache key); without a seed they are uncacheable.

The CA (Catani-Ahlgren) test ALWAYS runs inside vtt_arch: switching it off makes the routine fail. The CA statistic is bootstrap-only (there is no asymptotic p or df); only the ET and MARCH toggles are exposed.
The input is a fitted VAR, NOT a bare residual matrix: residuals alone give silently wrong LM auxiliary regressions (the vtt_check_fit gate blocks it).

univariate takes only False or True — the third documented value fails (blocked). The MARCH df = K^2(K+1)^2 h/4 grows fast with K, so a small sample gives low power. The wild-bootstrap p-values arrive as WBr_pv (recursive) or WBf_pv (fixed).
sources: Ahlgren, N. & Catani, P. (2016), 'Wild bootstrap tests for autocorrelation in vector autoregressive models', Statistical Papers, doi:10.1007/s00362-016-0744-0

Catani & Ahlgren 2016 (the combined bootstrap LM ARCH test); Eklund & Teräsvirta 2007 (CCC-ARCH LM); Lütkepohl 2006, New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis, sect. 16.5 (multivariate ARCH-LM); MacKinnon & White 1985 (HCCME)

cards.when: identifying a structural shock with an external series that is correlated with it and with nothing else -- high-frequency surprises, narrative records
cards.when_not: no credible external instrument exists; the instrument is weak, where the identification is not merely imprecise but invalid

alternatives.criterion: an ordering is defensible and no instrument exists
theory restricts the signs of responses
a credible external instrument exists

output_key_fields: irf: structural impulse responses to the identified shock
first_stage_f: instrument relevance -- the number that decides whether any of this holds
reliability: the instrument's correlation with the shock
conf_band: bootstrap bands respecting the two-stage structure
interpretation_traps: a WEAK instrument makes the identified responses badly biased and their bands far too narrow; report the first-stage F prominently, not in a footnote
the proxy identifies ONE shock, not the whole system; responses of other shocks are not identified and must not be reported as if they were
the instrument must be exogenous to all other shocks, which is untestable and is where the identification actually rests

cards.when: identifying structural shocks from the non-Gaussianity of the reduced-form residuals, without sign or timing restrictions
cards.when_not: the residuals are Gaussian, where the approach is not identified at all; the sample is too short for higher moments to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: an ordering is defensible
variance regimes are available
the residuals are demonstrably non-Gaussian

output_key_fields: b_matrix: the estimated structural impact matrix
irf: structural impulse responses
nongaussianity: per-residual diagnostics, the assumption everything rests on
j_statistic: overidentification test of the moment conditions
interpretation_traps: identification comes ENTIRELY from non-Gaussianity; with Gaussian residuals nothing is identified and the reported matrix is arbitrary -- check the diagnostic first
the shocks are identified only up to PERMUTATION and SIGN; labelling them economically is an additional, separate step
higher moments are estimated imprecisely, so identification can be weak even when the null of Gaussianity is rejected
sources: Keweloh 2021 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 39:772)

cards.when: VAR coefficients are biased in small samples and impulse-response bands built from asymptotics are badly wrong at long horizons
cards.when_not: the sample is very large, where the bias is negligible; the model is not a VAR

alternatives.criterion: large sample, short horizons
small sample, bias correction wanted
heteroskedastic or dependent residuals

output_key_fields: irf: bias-corrected impulse responses
bands: bootstrap confidence bands per horizon
bias_correction: the size of the adjustment applied
coverage_type: pointwise or joint, which is not the same thing
interpretation_traps: POINTWISE bands do not cover the whole response function simultaneously; reading a pointwise band as if it were joint overstates precision at every horizon
the bias correction can push a near-unit-root system into the explosive region, which is why the stationarity adjustment exists and must be applied
bootstrap bands inherit any misspecification of the VAR; they are not robust to a wrong lag order
sources: Kilian & Lutkepohl 2017, Structural Vector Autoregressive Analysis, ch.12
Hall 1992, The Bootstrap and Edgeworth Expansion

cards.method: Lag-augmented local projections with robust inference
cards.when: impulse responses without committing to a VAR, with inference that stays valid whether or not the variables have unit roots
cards.when_not: the horizon is short and a VAR is well specified, where the VAR is more efficient

alternatives.criterion: efficient when the VAR is correct
robust to misspecification but with size distortions at long horizons
valid inference regardless of persistence

output_key_fields: irf: the response per horizon
conf_band: bands valid under persistence
lag_augmentation: the extra lag that delivers the robustness
hac_bandwidth: the truncation used for the serial correlation
interpretation_traps: LAG AUGMENTATION is what makes the inference uniformly valid -- omitting the extra lag reintroduces exactly the size distortion the method removes
local-projection residuals are serially correlated at horizons beyond one by construction; HAC or the appropriate correction is mandatory
local projections are less efficient than a correctly specified VAR; the robustness is bought with wider bands

cards.when: the system's dynamics or shock variances change between regimes, and the regimes are latent rather than dated
cards.when_not: the regimes are known and dated (use dummies); the sample has too few regime switches for the transition probabilities to be estimated

alternatives.criterion: the regime is driven by an observed variable
change is gradual rather than discrete
discrete latent regimes

output_key_fields: params: regime-specific coefficients and covariances
smoothed_probabilities: probability of each regime at each date
transition_matrix: regime persistence
expected_duration: mean regime length
interpretation_traps: the LABEL SWITCHING problem means regimes are identified only up to permutation; interpreting 'regime 1' requires an explicit ordering rule
the likelihood is multimodal and estimation is sensitive to starting values; a single run is not a result
with few switches in sample the transition probabilities are estimated from a handful of transitions and are very imprecise

cards.when: identifying a shock as the one explaining most of the forecast-error variance of a variable, over a chosen horizon or frequency band
cards.when_not: you have a credible instrument or sign restriction; the target variable and horizon cannot be justified from theory

alternatives.criterion: an ordering is defensible
theory restricts signs
theory says a shock dominates a particular variable's variance

output_key_fields: b_vector: the identified impact vector
irf: responses to the identified shock
variance_share: the share it explains at each horizon
band: the frequency band, where spectral identification is used
interpretation_traps: the identified shock is defined BY THE TARGET AND HORIZON; changing either changes the shock, so both are identifying assumptions and must be justified
the maximising shock need not correspond to any economic shock -- it is a statistical construct that theory must license
over a long horizon the method converges to a permanent-component identification and loses its distinctness from long-run restrictions

cards.when: theory delivers both timing restrictions on impact and neutrality restrictions in the long run, and using both identifies more shocks than either alone
cards.when_not: the long-run restrictions rest on unit roots the data do not support; the system is too small for the combined restrictions to be over-identifying

alternatives.criterion: impact timing is all theory gives
neutrality is all theory gives
both are available and you want the extra identification

output_key_fields: b_matrix: the identified impact matrix
irf: structural responses
overidentification_test: where the restrictions exceed what is needed
long_run_matrix: the implied cumulative effects
interpretation_traps: LONG-RUN RESTRICTIONS ARE ESTIMATED FROM AN INFINITE-HORIZON EXTRAPOLATION of a finite sample; they are notoriously imprecise and small VAR misspecifications distort them badly
combining restrictions can over-identify the system, which is testable -- and the test is often ignored when it should be reported
a long-run restriction requires the relevant variable to be genuinely I(1); imposing it on a stationary variable is meaningless

cards.method: Panel and group local projections with Driscoll-Kraay errors
cards.when: estimating dynamic responses across many units, where cross-sectional dependence makes ordinary panel standard errors far too small
cards.when_not: there is one unit; the panel is too short in the time dimension for Driscoll-Kraay to be valid

alternatives.criterion: one time series
many units, common dynamics
responses differ by group and you want them separately

output_key_fields: irf: the pooled or per-group response
conf_band: bands robust to cross-sectional dependence
heterogeneity: variation of responses across units, where estimated
n_units, n_periods: the panel dimensions the inference rests on
interpretation_traps: Driscoll-Kraay standard errors need a LONG TIME DIMENSION; with short T they are badly undersized, which is the opposite of what they are used for
pooling imposes a common response; if the true responses are heterogeneous the pooled estimate is a weighted average that may match no unit
unit fixed effects in a dynamic panel introduce Nickell bias, which grows as T shrinks
sources: Jorda, Schularick & Taylor 2020 (Journal of Monetary Economics 112:22-40)
Driscoll & Kraay 1998 (Review of Economics and Statistics 80:549)
